outlook.statement: Global caustic prices have largely bottomed out, providing a stable base for recovery in Chlor Alkali segment. Full benefits of new electrolyser plant and hybrid renewable power project expected to reflect from FY27.

OPVC Pipes segment: Business pick up expected from Q3 FY27 as Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 funding resumes. Meaningful fund flows expected from Q2 FY27. Line 7 scheduled for Q2 FY27, completing Sri City site at 23,000 TPA.
OPVC pipes market size stood at ₹225 crore in FY26 and is projected to expand about fourfold to ₹1,000 crore by FY29, as per management estimates.

Management expects FY27 to be a materially stronger year than FY26. In the chlor alkali segment, stabilising realisations, efficiencies from the modernised facility and the commencement of hybrid power supply are expected to drive a marked improvement in profitability. For OPVC pipes, Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 has been approved with an FY27 allocation of ₹67,600 crore, and meaningful disbursements are expected from Q2 FY27. The Company has diversified its order book beyond the Mission, securing inclusion in multiple state-level projects.

Hybrid renewable energy project sourced through a dedicated SPV stands ready and awaits final transmission line clearances. Supply is expected to commence early in FY27, after which renewable sources will meet close to 55% of the Company's energy requirement, largely displacing coal-based power.

India's chemical industry long-run potential approaching USD 1 trillion by 2040, contingent on policy continuity, feedstock security and infrastructure development. OPVC pipes market valued at ₹225 crore in FY26, projected to reach about ₹1,000 crore by FY29.
outlook.period: Long-term (by 2040 for chemicals, by FY29 for OPVC)

outlook.statement: The Company plans to increase the share of renewable energy in its total energy consumption from 15% to 65%, significantly reducing its carbon footprint while enhancing long-term energy security and cost competitiveness, commencing from Q1 FY 2026-27.
Replacement of 30-year-old UHDE electrolysers with advanced INEOS electrolyser is expected to enhance production efficiency, reduce energy consumption, and lower maintenance costs.
Complete transition from furnace oil and diesel to Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) as a cleaner fuel strategy, achieving sustained reduction of SOx and SPM emissions.
The Company manages financial risk relating to the operations through internal risk reports which analyse exposure by degree and magnitude of risk.

The Board of Directors of the Parent company have recommended a final dividend of 12.50% (₹ 1.25 per Equity Share of ₹ 10 each) for the financial year 2025-26 which is subject to the approval of the shareholders in the forthcoming Annual General Meeting of the Parent Company.

risks: Chlor Alkali is a commoditised segment where realisations are driven by global price movements and cyclical factors beyond company control
Funding pauses under government programmes (e.g., Jal Jeevan Mission) can constrain OPVC Pipes market and slow tendering activity
Planned maintenance shutdowns (e.g., electrolyser replacement) can affect production volumes
Transmission clearance delays for hybrid renewable power project could defer energy cost savings
Forward-looking statements are inherently susceptible to risks and uncertainties; assumptions and predictions may not prove precise
Material decline in global caustic soda prices from oversupply or macroeconomic pressures directly affecting segment profitability
Escalating power costs compressing margins when external pricing is weak (energy is largest element of cost structure)
OPVC segment project execution tied closely to government funding cycles; delays in fund release, tendering or Cabinet-level approvals can defer demand
Investment ahead of demand realisation can leave capacity underutilised and weigh on operating efficiency
Structural surplus in chlor alkali industry with capacity growing ~9% annually against ~4% demand growth
Import dependence in petrochemical intermediates and speciality chemicals sustaining trade deficit
Limited backward integration and concentration in commodity grades restricting value-chain advancement
Feedstock constraints and logistical inefficiencies influencing production costs and operational efficiency
Regulatory non-compliance risk (SEBI LODR) - fined for delay in independent director appointment and shareholder approval
Energy cost volatility - mitigated by renewable energy transition and long-term hybrid power supply agreements
Environmental compliance risk - addressed by transition to LNG and emission reduction initiatives
The Company does not have commodity price risk nor does the Company engage in hedging activities.

other_notable: Chlor Alkali division: First in India to implement membrane cell technology (1985), first globally to introduce ultrafiltration for brine clarification (2003), patented world's first fully enclosed negative pressure system for chlorine containment (2011), first Indian plant to conduct carbon footprint study (2013), first chlor-alkali plant in India certified to ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 (2014), patented zero-waste process converting brine sludge to bricks (2017), patented technology to remove trace iodide from brine (2023), transitioned to LNG and migrated to SAP S/4 HANA (2024).

OPVC Pipes division: First Indian manufacturer of OPVC pipes up to 630 mm diameter (2021), BIS certificate of appreciation for zero failures (2021), largest operational OPVC capacity in India (20,000 TPA as of FY26), only Indian manufacturer producing OPVC pipes up to 630 mm diameter.
